overview: Credit Corp Group is Australia's largest provider of responsible financial services to the credit-impaired consumer segment, purchasing defaulted consumer debt ledgers (PDLs) and collecting on them, providing agency collection services to corporate clients, and offering consumer lending products to borrowers with limited access to mainstream credit. The group operates across Australia and New Zealand (debt buying, collection services and consumer lending under the Wallet Wizard, CarStart and Wizit brands), the United States (debt buying, now a major earnings contributor), and, as of FY2026/27, a newly launched consumer lending operation in the United Kingdom. ASX-listed since 2000, with a June fiscal year end.

business_model.summary: Credit Corp buys charged-off consumer debt portfolios (PDLs) from banks, telcos and utilities at a discount to face value, then collects on them over multi-year periods using in-house analytics, call centres (Australia, NZ, Philippines, US) and structured repayment arrangements; it also earns fee-for-service agency collection income (NCML, Baycorp, Collection House brands) and net interest income from its own consumer loan book (Wallet Wizard, CarStart, Wizit, and now UK lending). Revenue recognition on PDLs is effectively an amortising yield on the purchase price re-estimated against expected future collections (accounting-estimate-sensitive), which is different from a simple cash-collections model.

revenue_streams.name: US Debt Buying (PDL collections)
revenue_streams.note: NPAT contribution ~$55.9m in FY2026, up 57% YoY; became the largest segment by NPAT

revenue_streams.name: AU/NZ Debt Buying and Collection Services (PDL + agency collections)
revenue_streams.note: NPAT $23.4m FY2026, up 5% -- first growth since FY2022

revenue_streams.name: AU/NZ Consumer Lending (Wallet Wizard, CarStart, Wizit)
revenue_streams.note: NPAT $26.2m FY2026, up 3%; record $424m lending volume, $510m gross loan book

revenue_streams.name: UK Consumer Lending (new, launched July 2026)
revenue_streams.note: Pre-revenue in FY2026; first loans issued July 2026; medium-term aspiration of $150-200m book

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: B2B clients (banks, finance companies, telcos, utilities, government) sell debt portfolios and outsource collections; B2C consumers are the credit-impaired borrowers/debtors on both the collections and lending sides
business_model.geographic_mix: Group revenue $586m FY2026 (up 7%); income-generating assets $1,294.9m; $13.8bn face value of receivables globally across Australia (1,149 staff), Philippines (554, offshore support), US (412), New Zealand (102) and a new UK operation (6 staff)

main_competitors: Encore Capital Group / Midland Credit Management (US)
Cash Converters / other subprime lenders (AU consumer lending)
Incumbent UK sub-prime lenders (UK, market currently under-served after several exited)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest debt buyer/collector in Australia and NZ by a wide margin (post-Collection House acquisition in 2022); a top-tier but not #1 player in the US market (behind PRA Group and Encore Capital), with an operating platform now benchmarking close to listed US competitors on asset turnover; a leading credit-impaired consumer lender in Australia via Wallet Wizard; a new entrant in UK sub-prime lending

moat_factors.description: 14+ years of collections and repayment data feed statistical pricing and credit models that support both PDL bid pricing and loan underwriting; increasingly augmented by AI/LLM tools for collections efficiency

Consistently the lowest external dispute resolution (EDR) complaint rate among larger Australian debt buyers and top-rated hardship response; this reputation is itself a competitive advantage in winning forward-flow and portfolio sale panels from risk-averse bank/telco clients

Only major domestic player with meaningful scale across three countries (AU/NZ, US, and now UK) and three business lines (debt buying, agency collections, consumer lending), reducing reliance on any single credit cycle or geography

Access to all but one of the major US financial-services debt-selling panels; disciplined bidding rather than lowest-price-wins keeps it competitive but not always the largest buyer in any given period

Investment-grade discipline (walking away from overpriced PDL vintages, as seen in FY2026 US market) protects returns but can cede volume/share to less disciplined competitors during hot pricing markets

weaknesses: Not the largest player in the more competitive and larger US debt-buying market (behind PRA Group, Encore Capital)
AU/NZ debt buying segment collections had contracted for four straight years (FY2022-FY2025) before returning to modest growth in FY2026, partly aided by a one-off bank book acquisition
New UK lending business carries execution and regulatory risk in an unfamiliar jurisdiction with a history of forcing incumbents out via adverse regulatory action
Consumer lending margins are being invested into growth (marketing, product diversification via Wizit) which suppresses near-term segment earnings growth

growth_drivers: US debt buying: operational improvement (legal collections channel changes, up 36% in Q4 FY2026) driving asset turnover toward parity with listed US competitors, expected to sustain segment NPAT growth into FY2027 even as purchasing volumes are guided down

UK consumer lending market entry: large, currently under-served credit-impaired lending market after incumbent sub-prime lenders exited under regulatory pressure; medium-term aspiration of a $150-200m loan book, long-term target exceeding $400m

AU/NZ consumer lending diversification: Wizit digital credit card (17% of new lending customers in FY2026) and CarStart broadening the addressable customer base beyond the flagship Wallet Wizard cash-loan product; record $510m closing loan book

AU/NZ debt buying market recovery: signs the multi-year contraction in market-wide PDL sale volumes has ended, with aggregate unsecured consumer credit growing again and more credit providers moving to sell down receivables
AI/LLM deployment across collections operations (call summarisation, dialling optimisation, quality assurance) to lift collector productivity and reduce cost-to-collect
Continued industry consolidation in Australian debt collection favoring the largest, best-capitalized, most compliant player

business.description: PDL pricing, collection rates and consumer repayment capacity are directly tied to the credit cycle and cost-of-living pressures; a deterioration in consumer finances or unemployment could reduce collection yields on existing ledgers priced under different assumptions

US business now the largest segment; success depends on continuing to close the operational gap to entrenched, larger competitors (PRA Group, Encore) while maintaining purchase-price discipline in an increasingly competitive/expensive PDL market; FY2026 saw purchasing volumes fall short of expectations due to price discipline

New geography, new regulatory regime, unproven local team and systems; management explicitly notes prior UK sub-prime lenders failed under responsible-lending law changes and withdrew capital -- Credit Corp is entering that same regulatory environment

business.risk: Customer/client concentration and reliance on bank/telco debt sale volumes
business.description: AU/NZ PDL supply depends on major banks' and utilities' willingness to sell charged-off debt; banks have at times delayed sales or increased in-house collections, shrinking available portfolio volume

Record $510m consumer loan book concentrated in credit-impaired borrowers; even with short loan duration and upfront lifetime loss provisioning, a sharp downturn in borrower serviceability could increase losses

financial.risk: PDL carrying value / accounting estimate risk
financial.description: Purchased debt ledger revenue and NPAT are sensitive to re-estimation of future collections and useful-life assumptions; the company has previously flagged NPAT impacts from changes in PDL accounting estimates (useful life) as a distinct line item in its own reporting
Debt buying and lending are funded substantially by debt facilities; rising interest rates increase funding costs and can compress spreads on both PDL investments and the consumer loan book
US and now UK operations create translation and economic FX exposure on segment earnings reported in AUD

regulatory.description: ASIC and consumer-credit regulators continue to scrutinize debt collection and hardship practices; Credit Corp markets its low EDR complaint rate as a competitive strength, implying the regulatory bar for the industry is rising

Management's own commentary notes UK regulatory tightening (responsible lending laws) drove multiple incumbent sub-prime lenders out of the market via adverse regulatory action and claims liabilities -- the same regime Credit Corp is now entering

regulatory.risk: US consumer protection / FDCPA and state-level debt collection rules
regulatory.description: US collections activity, including the expanded legal/attorney collection channel, is subject to federal (CFPB/FDCPA) and state debt-collection laws that could tighten or add compliance cost

regulatory.risk: Consumer credit licensing across three jurisdictions
regulatory.description: Operating regulated lending and collection businesses simultaneously in Australia, US and UK multiplies licensing, capital and compliance obligations

macro.description: Higher rates raise the group's own funding costs and pressure borrower serviceability, while also affecting PDL pricing/discount rates used to value ledgers

Elevated cost-of-living pressures affect both the collectability of existing debt ledgers and the credit quality of new consumer loans, though short loan duration and provisioning partly mitigate this

A sharp economic downturn would likely increase debt-sale supply (more charge-offs) but simultaneously reduce collection rates and consumer repayment capacity -- a double-edged cyclical exposure inherent to the debt-purchasing model

FY2026 saw significant price growth in the US PDL market that suppressed Credit Corp's purchasing growth as it maintained investment discipline -- a sustained seller's market could constrain future US segment growth

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian debt-buying market showing signs of recovery after a multi-year contraction in market-wide PDL sale volumes, with aggregate unsecured consumer credit growing again; US debt-purchasing market offers larger volumes but has seen elevated pricing/competition; UK sub-prime consumer lending market described by management as in 'disequilibrium' with unmet demand after incumbent exits, a structural opportunity for a well-capitalized, compliant new entrant
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — debt purchasing volumes and collection yields are geared to the credit cycle and consumer financial stress, though the model has some natural counter-cyclical supply (more charge-offs available to buy in downturns) balanced against lower collection rates
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — affects funding costs on debt facilities backing both PDL purchases and the consumer loan book, and influences the discount rates used in ledger valuation
key_input_costs: Purchase price of debt ledgers (PDL pricing)
Collections labour/call-centre costs (AU, NZ, Philippines, US, UK)

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results: record NPAT of $105.5m (+12% YoY), revenue $586m (+7%), EPS 155.0c (+12%), post-tax operating cash flow $427m (+11%); dividend raised 14% to 77.5cps fully franked; ROE improved to 13.1% from 11.1%
US segment NPAT rose 57% to $55.9m, becoming Credit Corp's largest segment, on a 24% rise in collections and improved asset-turnover benchmarking near listed US competitors
FY2027 guidance issued: NPAT of $110-118m (+4-12% YoY), reflecting an expected decline in US PDL purchasing volumes offset by continued operational/collection improvements and lending growth

Share price reaction was subdued/slightly negative (down modestly, and reported down as much as ~6-7% in some sessions) despite the record result, as investors focused on the more moderate FY2027 growth guidance and lower expected US purchasing volumes
Credit Corp issued its first UK consumer loans in early July 2026 (start of FY2027), completing the acquisition of a licensed UK lending entity, systems build and local team recruitment during FY2026
Board leadership transition flagged: long-serving Chair Eric Dodd (17 years on the Board, 5+ years as Chair) is departing, described in the FY2026 Annual Report as 'one of my final duties as Chair'
AU/NZ debt buying segment returned to collections and NPAT growth (both +4-5%) for the first time since FY2022, aided by a large one-off credit card run-off book acquired from a major bank
Consumer lending achieved record loan volumes ($424m, +15%) and record closing loan book ($510m gross), with the new Wizit digital credit card reaching 17% of new lending customers

items.vs_prior: new guidance (implies +4% to +12% YoY growth vs FY2026's $105.5m)
items.notes: Growth expected to be driven by continued US operational improvement and AU/NZ/UK lending growth even as US PDL purchasing volumes are expected to decline
Driven by continued growth in existing AU/NZ products (Wallet Wizard, Wizit, CarStart) plus early contribution from new UK lending operations
Reflects continued investment-discipline in the face of elevated US PDL pricing; management expects operational improvement to nonetheless sustain segment NPAT growth
Long-term aspiration exceeding $400m; management targets minimizing start-up losses given the current period of excess unmet demand in the UK sub-prime segment

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Thomas Beregi highlighted record group NPAT and cash flow, a 57% surge in US segment earnings from operational improvement (legal-channel changes, improving asset turnover toward parity with listed US peers), and the strategic significance of entering the UK market as a large, currently under-served opportunity where several incumbent lenders were forced out by tightening responsible-lending regulation. Management explicitly flagged that FY2026 US purchasing fell short of expectations due to maintained investment discipline amid 'significant price growth,' and that FY2027 US purchasing volumes are expected to be lower, with earnings growth instead coming from operational improvement. Outgoing Chair Eric Dodd emphasized the long-term strategic diversification into lending and US/UK debt buying as having reduced reliance on the historically core AU/NZ debt-buying business, which now produces well under half of group NPAT.

bull_case: Diversified, three-country, three-business-line model (debt buying, agency collections, consumer lending) reduces reliance on any single credit cycle or geography, with non-AU/NZ-debt-buying segments now generating over three-quarters of group earnings

US segment delivered 57% NPAT growth in FY2026 and is closing the operational gap to larger listed peers (PRA Group, Encore Capital) on asset turnover, suggesting further re-rating potential as the platform matures

UK entry targets a large, currently under-served sub-prime lending market where incumbents were forced out by regulation, giving Credit Corp a potential first-mover/responsible-operator advantage and a long-dated growth option (medium-term $150-200m book, long-term $400m+)

Consistently the lowest external dispute resolution complaint rate among larger Australian debt buyers, a compliance/reputation moat that supports client (bank/telco) trust and lowers regulatory risk relative to peers

Record operating cash flow ($427m, +11%) and rising ROE (13.1% from 11.1%) with a growing, well-covered fully franked dividend (77.5cps, +14%) support shareholder returns alongside reinvestment for growth
bear_case: FY2027 NPAT guidance of $110-118m (+4-12%) represents a marked deceleration from FY2026's momentum, driven by an expected decline in US PDL purchasing volumes -- the market reacted to this softer outlook by marking the stock down despite record FY2026 results

UK expansion carries real execution and regulatory risk: management's own commentary notes that prior UK sub-prime lenders suffered adverse regulatory action and material claim liabilities under tightening responsible-lending law -- the exact regime Credit Corp is now entering with an unproven local operation

US debt-buying market has seen 'significant price growth' compressing purchase economics, and Credit Corp is not the largest player against better-capitalized incumbents (PRA Group, Encore Capital), so continued share gains are not guaranteed

Business model has inherent credit-cycle risk: an economic downturn increases the supply of charged-off debt but can simultaneously suppress collection rates on both existing ledgers and the consumer loan book, and PDL revenue/accounting estimates can be volatile as useful-life and collection assumptions are revised

AU/NZ core debt-buying segment only just returned to growth in FY2026 after four years of contraction, partly aided by a one-off bank portfolio acquisition, raising questions about the sustainability of that recovery absent similar one-offs
